metadata.summary: Oncofetal programs are often co-opted in high-grade gliomas and represent tumor cell vulnerabilities for therapeutic exploitation. Here, we integrate single nucleus RNA-seq and single-cell ATAC sequencing data generated from germinal matrix and cortical plate regions macrodissected from prenatal and postnatal developing brain autopsy tissue, creating an expanded spatiotemporal multi-omic dataset of gliogenic progenitors. The integrated multi-omics data includes previously published data (Ramos et al, Nature Commun 2022; Herring et al, Cell 2022) as well as newly-generated and herein deposited data. We use this dataset to interrogate oncofetal cell state composition in grade 4 gliomas across several published high-grade glioma / glioblastoma (GBM) datasets to uniquely assess tumor heterogeneity related to infiltrative biology near the margin and disease recurrence, in addition to genomic drivers. Our analyses reveal the preferential enrichment of glial intermediate progenitor cell (gIPC)-like cell state in GBM, most reminiscent of third-trimester germinal matrix gIPC progenitors, across tumor regions and in recurrence, irrespective of EGFR amplification status.

observations.text:
ObjectiveThe objective of this study was to identify the demographic and clinical predictors of statin intolerance among patients prescribed statins for the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease during the first two years following the first recorded prescription, using real-world data.

MethodsThis study used the Electronic Practice Based Research Network Linked Dataset. An operational definition based on muscle symptoms and creatine kinase levels was applied to identify patients with statin intolerance. Descriptive and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed using R software. All variables identified a priori as potential predictors were included in the initial model, and backward stepwise selection using the Akaike Information Criterion was performed across the imputed datasets to identify a parsimonious final model.

ResultsOverall, 4,016 patients accounting for 60,873 visits were included in the analysis. About 3.5% of patients were statin intolerant. After adjusting for all other variables, higher odds of statin intolerance were observed among female or other gender patients (AOR 1.5, 95% CI 1.0 - 2.2), patients residing in Socio-Economic Indexes for Australia (SEIFA) area based socioeconomic advantage and disadvantage (IRSAD) category 8 or 9 (AOR 3.4, 95% CI 2.0 - 5.8), and patients with three or more selected comorbidities (AOR 6.4, 95% CI 2.2 - 18.3). A similar direction of associations was seen in the final model.

ConclusionGender, IRSAD, and the number of selected comorbidities were associated with statin intolerance. However, these findings should be interpreted in the context of the operational EHR based definition of statin intolerance. Further validation in other populations and settings is required before these predictors can be considered for clinical application.
observations.title: Predictors of statin intolerance among statin users in primary care using real-world data

observations.text:
PurposeThis study aimed to identify the demographic and clinical predictors of statin adherence among patients prescribed statins for the primary prevention of CVD during the first two years following their first recorded statin prescription, using real-world data.

MethodsThe Electronic Practice Based Research Network Linked Dataset was used in this study. Statin adherence was calculated using a modified proportion of days covered (PDC), based on prescribing data from the date of the first recorded statin prescription to the to the last recorded visit within the two years observation period. Patients with a PDC [≥] 80% were classified as adherent. All analyses were performed using R software. Descriptive analyses and multivariate logistic regression were performed. Backward stepwise selection guided by the Akaike Information Criterion was used to derive a parsimonious final model.

ResultsOverall, 3,432 patients accounting for 57,227 visits were included. The mean PDC was 91.6% ({+/-}22.2%), and 72.0% of patients were classified as adherent. Higher odds of adherence was observed among patients aged over 65 years (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 1.4, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.1 - 1.8), those residing in Socio-Economic Indexes for Australia 2021 Index of Relative Socio-Economic Advantage and Disadvantage category 3 (AOR 2.1, 95% CI 1.6 - 2.9), those prescribed three medications, including a statin (AOR 1.8, 95% CI 1.3 - 2.4) and those with one selected comorbidity (AOR 1.4, 95% CI 1.1 - 1.7), compared with their respective reference categories. Patients prescribed two or more statin types had lower odds of adherence (AOR 0.7, 95% CI 0.5 - 0.9).

ConclusionsAge, area level socioeconomic status, and the number of prescribed medications, selected comorbidities and statin types were associated with statin adherence. However, adherence was estimated from prescribing rather than dispensing data, and the model demonstrated modest discrimination. Further validation in independent populations is needed to validate these associations.
observations.title: Predictors of statin adherence among statin users in primary care using real-world data

metadata.summary: Microexons are extremely short exons that are highly conserved in vertebrates and are essential for normal brain development. Their small size poses a challenge for canonical exon-definition splice site recognition, which typically relies on spliceosomal interactions across standard length exons. Here, we determine the sequence and RNA structural features of neural microexons in humans in comparison with chickens. We find that neural microexons share intronic features that extend the functional distance between the branchpoint and the 3’ splice site, including distal positioning and lengthening of polypyrimidine tracts. Using experimental RNA structure-probing on a subset of neural microexons, we show that the branchpoint-to-splice site region is unusually accessible and relatively unpaired compared to other exon classes. However, we find little support for shared RNA secondary structures between orthologous human and chicken precursor RNAs despite high sequence conservation. Using the chick embryo as a developmental model, we demonstrate that a subset of neural microexons undergo dynamic, stage-specific regulation during brain development that correlates with expression of known microexon regulators, SRRM4 and NOVA1. Our data suggest that neural microexon splicing fluctuates during brain development and may rely on an extended polypyrimidine tract and structural accessibility for splicing efficiency, rather than conserved secondary structures.

observations.text: Searching petabase-scale repositories of raw sequencing data such as the NIH Sequence Read Archive (SRA) could unlock biological insights that remain inaccessible. Existing sequence-search methods either do not scale well or rely on exact $k$-mer matching that is brittle to genomic variation, which is high both within and across species and is further compounded by sequencing error. We recast sequence search as dense retrieval: we learn sequence embeddings whose inner-product similarity ranks locally aligned sequences above unaligned ones. We introduce LOCALE, an encoder trained with an InfoNCE objective on biologically informed augmentations: overlapping crops of parent sequences corrupted with substitutions, insertions, and deletions. This training recipe, rather than a specialized architecture, consistently induces variation-robust representations across four encoders spanning three tokenization schemes, improving Recall@$R_q$ by 7--39 points at 10% genomic variation. On a 50-accession SRA benchmark LOCALE retains 63.2% Recall@$R_q$ at 10% variation while existing k-mer indexes and DNA embedding methods fall below 35%, and on the full 4,571-accession MetaGraph benchmark (296 Gbp, 2.06 billion vectors) it achieves 4.5x the AUPRC of MetaGraph, the state-of-the-art k-mer index, with a single-node GPU IVF-PQ index retaining a 3.6x advantage at MetaGraph's query latency. Our encoder and training strategy generalize to real biological variance: on a cross-genotype Hepatitis B task, querying reads from one genotype against accessions of another with >8% natural divergence, LOCALE reaches 0.813 Recall@R_q versus 0.518 for MetaGraph.

metadata.summary: Direct cardiac reprogramming relies on a combination of canonical cardiac transcription factors, typically consisting of Mef2c, Gata4, and Tbx5 (MGT). However, successful lineage conversion requires additional endogenous factors that coordinate the chromatin and transcriptional changes underlying fibroblast-to-cardiomyocyte conversion. Here, we identify Activating Transcription Factor 7 (Atf7) as a critical supporting factor that enables efficient direct cardiac reprogramming. Loss of function studies in primary murine cardiac fibroblasts demonstrate that Atf7 knockdown markedly reduces MGT mediated reprogramming efficiency, with the strongest impairment occurring when Atf7 is depleted during the early priming window of days 0–3. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that Atf7 knockdown disrupts the induction of cardiomyocyte gene programs while derepressing fibroblast  and extracellular matrix–associated pathways, shifting the global expression profile toward a non reprogrammed state. These findings support a bifunctional regulatory role of Atf7 in promoting cardiomyocyte-specific gene activation while repressing fibroblast-associated transcriptional networks.

metadata.summary: Ponatinib is a potent tyrosine kinase inhibitor and primarily used in the treatment of chronic myelogenous leukemia and Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Due to the potential vascular side effects including cardiotoxicity (CTX), its broad anti-cancer capability is restricted, while replaceable better alternative is currently not available. Investigating ponatinib CTX is for getting a better understanding of the fundamental molecular mechanisms which are crucial for developing innovative cardiovascular protection. We have established a ponatinib-induced CTX mouse model, specifically, evaluated long-term effects of ponatinib on cardiac structural and function and demonstrated cardioprotective effects in inducible cardiomyocyte-specific ROCK1 and ROCK2 knockout mouse hearts (DKO). To explore the mechanisms underlying the cardioprotective effects in DKO hearts, single nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) study has been implemented.  Results have revealed that double ROCK deletion in cardiomyocytes mitigates ponatinib-induced CTX through suppressing pathological remodeling of cardiomyocytes and nonmyocytes.

metadata.summary: Atherosclerotic plaque rupture is a major cause of myocardial infarction and stroke. However, the precise drivers of plaque destabilisation remain elusive. We hypothesised that antigen-driven, autoimmune-like T cell responses are central to the destabilisation and rupture of atherosclerotic plaques. To dissect T cell responses specifically in unstable compared to stable plaques, we leveraged near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) imaging-guided dissection of human carotid plaques and our tandem stenosis model in mice. We applied single-cell multi-omics to study T cell differentiation states and T cell receptor (TCR) repertoires. T cell responses in unstable versus stable atherosclerosis were distinct. Unstable human plaques contained highly expanded, autoimmune-like CD8+ T cells with markedly increased cytotoxic signatures, reduced exhaustion and distinct clonal repertoires compared to stable regions. Most plaque CD8+ T cells exhibited a pronounced tissue-resident transcriptional program. Autoimmune-like cytotoxic and tissue-resident CD8+ T cell responses were also evident in murine atherosclerosis, where restricting the activation of antigen-driven CD8+ T cells prevented plaque destabilisation.

observations.text: Efficient lipid design under limited experimental budgets is a central challenge in computational chemistry and drug discovery. We introduce LEAF (Lipid Evolutionary Adaptive Framework), a matched-budget protocol for testing whether language-model proposers improve combinatorial molecular search relative to classical baselines. The study uses a 30,044-candidate ionizable-lipid space, a frozen Gaussian-process oracle fitted to experimental potency labels, and a separate active-learning surrogate. Four language models evaluated over eight seeds and three splits show no significant improvement over genetic-algorithm or random-search baselines. For Llama 8B, 79.1% of acquisition-selected queries repeat previously evaluated archive members. Removing duplicates reduces the performance gap on some splits but increases proposal cost and can prevent budget exhaustion. Larger models reduce duplication without establishing superiority or equivalence. Exploratory scored prompts and stricter novelty controls yield positive median differences against the genetic algorithm, yet wide intervals and shared-seed dependence preclude stronger conclusions. A validated single-assay reanalysis preserves the chemotype-cold deficit at a smaller numerical scale, and exploratory expected hypervolume improvement does not reverse the result. Follow-up checks address whether proposers genuinely use injected evidence. These checks include a zero-shot leakage probe, rank-only and chain-of-thought-rationale prompts, a score-shuffle perturbation, an evidence-conflict probe, and a genuine reasoning-mode proposer. They show measurable engagement with supplied information without a corresponding performance gain. LEAF isolates proposal quality as the experimental variable and documents a concrete failure mode of zero-shot LLM proposers under controlled budgets.
observations.title: Do LLM Proposers Improve Budgeted Search for Ionizable Lipids?

metadata.summary: Non-infectious granulomatous diseases, including sarcoidosis, lack targeted, steroid-sparing therapies to disrupt the persistent immune cell aggregates that drive chronic tissue morbidity. Integrating multi-organ single-cell RNA sequencing with spatial transcriptomics, we identify conserved macrophage-specific induction of osteopontin (OPN) across human skin, lung, and heart lesions. Mechanistically, we show that local tissue coagulation acts as a functional checkpoint, where proteolytic cleavage of OPN by tissue thrombin generates OPN fragments that activate macrophages through α4 integrin, which amplifies macrophage OPN expression and establishes a feed-forward circuit that sustains granuloma stability. In mouse models, genetic or pharmacologic disruption of this coagulation-immune axis, including the repurposed direct thrombin inhibitor dabigatran and thrombin cleavage-blocking OPN antibodies, reduces granuloma formation and promotes resolution of established chronic lesions. Together, these findings identify a thrombin-dependent feed-forward coagulation–immune circuit that maintains granuloma stability and provides multiple therapeutically actionable targets for non-infectious granulomatous disease.

metadata.summary: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury triggers the recruitment of inflammatory cells, including neutrophils and monocytes. Currently, effective treatment strategies are not available for this widely occurring harmful condition. Using metabololipidomics, we uncovered relative reductions in the pro-resolving lipid mediator Resolvin-D1 (RvD1) early after reperfusion in both mouse and human transplanted hearts, and that exogenous treatment led to elevated tissue levels of RvD1. By intravital two-photon microscopy, we discovered that that pre-operative instillation of RvD1 into the donor heart or peri-operative systemic recipient RvD1 treatment reduced recruitment of neutrophils. Mechanistically, we found that RvD1 provides protection by signaling through Alx/Fpr2 on donor monocytes, which reduces their production of IL-1b, attenuating intravascular neutrophil aggregation and extravasation.  After allogeneic transplantation, peri-operative RvD1 treatment reduces myeloid cell recruitment, abrogates macrophage pro-inflammatory signaling within cardiac allografts, and significantly prolongs graft survival. This study defines the mechanistic basis of a therapeutic strategy that modulates inflammatory responses during myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury and provides a platform for the design of clinical trials.

observations.title: Activating resolution mitigates inflammation after heart transplantation in mice and prolongs graft survival

Bulk RNA-sequencing of archival FFPE tissues were performed. The objective of this study was to determine differentially expressed genes (DEG) and affected biological processes in placental tissue from pregnancies complicated by fetal LSOL with and without chronic forms of placental histopathology.

Matched RNA-seq and ribosome-protected fragment libraries allow changes in mRNA abundance to be separated from changes in ribosome occupancy and translational efficiency. metadata.summary: The molecular and cellular processes leading to aortic aneurysm development in Marfan syndrome (MFS) remain poorly understood. We examined the changes of aortic cell populations and gene expression in MFS. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) on ascending aortic aneurysm tissues from patients with MFS (n=3) and age-matched non-aneurysmal control tissues from cardiac donors and recipients (n=4). The expression of key molecules was confirmed by immunostaining. Diverse populations of smooth muscle cells (SMCs), fibroblasts, and endothelial cell (EC) were detected in the aortic wall. Aortic tissues from MFS showed alterations of cell populations with increased de-differentiated proliferative SMCs compared to controls. Furthermore, there was a downregulation of MYOCD and MYH11 in SMCs, and an upregulation of COL1A1/2 in fibroblasts in MFS samples compared to controls. We also examined TGF-β signaling, an important pathway in aortic homeostasis. We found that TGFB1 was significantly upregulated in two fibroblast clusters in MFS tissues. However, TGF-β receptor genes (predominantly TGFBR2) and SMAD genes were downregulated in SMCs, fibroblasts, and ECs, indicating impairment in TGF-β signaling in MFS. Despite upregulation of TGFB1, the rest of the canonical TGF-β pathway was consistently downregulated in MFS, indicating a potential compromise of TGF-β signaling and lack of stimulus for SMC differentiation.

observations.text:
PurposeEarly and reliable disease prediction from structured clinical data remains challenging when datasets are small, highly imbalanced, and contain limited positive disease cases. Conventional machine learning (ML) and deep learning approaches often struggle to capture clinically meaningful relationships under such low-data representation conditions due to weak statistical associations between features and prediction targets. This study proposes a clinically grounded Distil GPT2-based table-to-text framework for disease prediction using structured healthcare datasets, motivated by the contextual reasoning capability of GPT models to better capture clinically meaningful relationships when statistical learning alone becomes insufficient due to limited data availability.

MethodsStructured clinical records were transformed into physician-style textual descriptions and enriched through GPT4-generated medical paraphrasing to improve minority-class representation while preserving clinical meaning. Both the original and generated clinical texts were used to fine-tune a Distil GPT2 model across four public healthcare datasets, including heart disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and thyroid cancer recurrence. Gradient-based explainable AI analysis was additionally incorporated to identify clinically important features influencing prediction outcomes.

ResultsThe proposed framework demonstrated consistently strong predictive performance across four clinical datasets, achieving average precision, specificity, sensitivity, and F1-score of 0.96, 0.97, 0.96, and 0.96, respectively. The model achieved improved sensitivity, stronger generalization, and more stable predictive behavior compared with traditional ML, deep learning, transformer-based, and GAN-augmented approaches. Importantly, the framework consistently emphasized clinically meaningful variables even under severe class imbalance, where conventional ML and neural network models often struggled to identify key clinically relevant relationships.

ConclusionThe proposed Distil GPT2-based tableto-text framework provides a practical and clinically interpretable approach for disease prediction from limited structured healthcare data. By integrating contextual clinical reasoning with explainable prediction mechanisms, the framework suggests strong potential for early risk detection, transparent clinical decision support, and reliable deployment in real-world data-scarce healthcare settings.

metadata.summary: Background: Direct reprogramming of cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) into induced cardiomyocytes (iCMs) holds promise as a therapeutic strategy for heart regeneration. Post-myocardial infarction (MI), resident quiescent CFs (QCFs) activate and differentiate into myofibroblasts (MFs) in the infarcted region that drive pathological cardiac fibrosis. Converting these injury-activated MFs into iCMs could simultaneously alleviate fibrosis and replenish lost cardiomyocytes. However, whether the marked heterogeneity of CFs in the infarcted heart—and in particular the activation of QCFs into MFs—creates an intrinsic barrier that limits the reprogramming of these injury-activated MFs remains unknown. Methods: To define the molecular basis of this heterogeneity, we purified PDGFRα⁺ cardiac fibroblasts and used Postn lineage tracing to distinguish injury-activated MFs from quiescent CFs, enabling matched comparison of their reprogramming competence and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) profiling of post-MI CF subpopulations. A targeted in vitro shRNA screen was conducted against 9 MF-enriched TFs as candidate molecular barriers for cardiac reprogramming. The lead candidate was validated in mouse MFs, QCFs, human iPSC-derived MFs, primary human cardiac fibroblasts, and in vivo using dual-recombinase-mediated lineage tracing. Mechanistic insights were gained through integrated bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq and Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag), together with functional assays including DNA-binding–deficient and domain-swap MEOX1 mutants. Results: We identified the upregulated transcription factor MEOX1—a known fibrosis determinant downstream of the key post-MI cytokines TGF-β1 and IL-1β—as the principal molecular barrier responsible for the profound reprogramming resistance of MFs. MEOX1 knockdown markedly enhanced reprogramming efficiency in both mouse and human MFs and enabled GATA4-free reprogramming combinations. This inhibition depended on MEOX1’s transcriptional activation activity, as disrupting its DNA-binding domain or fusing it to a repressor domain rescued reprogramming. Integrated scRNA-seq and CUT&Tag analyses revealed that MEOX1 binds and stabilizes a fibrotic, MF-defining transcriptional program that antagonizes the cardiogenic program, while also modulating the inflammatory response; its knockdown disrupted this fibrotic network to favor iCM fate acquisition. Using stringent dual-recombinase lineage tracing, we demonstrated that MEOX1 knockdown enables highly efficient in vivo MF-to-iCM conversion, leading to significant reductions in cardiac fibrosis and substantial improvement in cardiac function after MI. Conclusions: Our study identifies the pathological upregulation of MEOX1 as a key mechanism underlying the reprogramming resistance of post-MI MFs, in both mouse and human. Overcoming this barrier achieves unprecedented, lineage-confirmed in vivo reprogramming efficiency, thereby addressing a significant obstacle for the clinical translation of in situ reprogramming therapies. Data included in this Series comprise the original bulk RNA-seq datasets of MGTM-reprogrammed mouse cardiac fibroblasts with control or Meox1 knockdown and with control vector/GFP or MEOX1 overexpression; RNA-seq datasets from human iPSCs, iPSC-derived cardiac fibroblasts, and iPSC-derived myofibroblasts; scRNA-seq datasets from MGTM-induced iCM cultures and normal or day-3 post-MI mouse hearts; MEOX1 CUT&Tag data; and the newly added three-biological-replicate bulk RNA-seq dataset comparing MGTM + shCtrl with MGTM + shMeox1 used for the revised manuscript.

observations.title: Overcoming Intrinsic Barriers in Myofibroblasts Permits Efficient Cardiac Reprogramming Post-Infarction

observations.text: Background: The anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) is consistently implicated in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). ACC variability, including its most variable structure, the paracingulate sulcus (PCGS), has been known since the late 1800s, and since then, has been linked to cognitive control, impulsivity, and psychiatric conditions comorbid with ADHD, including autism spectrum disorder and schizophrenia. Yet, the role of the PCGS in ADHD remains unexamined at the individual level. Methods: We characterized PCGS incidence, asymmetry, and morphology in 247 children and adolescents (144 ADHD: 10.9 +/- 2.73 years old, 75% male; 103 neurotypical: 12.2 +/- 3.17 years old, 50% male) from the ADHD-200 dataset. The PCGS was manually identified in FreeSurfer cortical surface reconstructions. Morphometric measures, including sulcal length, depth, and cortical thickness, were extracted and normalized to hemisphere-wide variables. Between-group analyses tested whether PCGS presence, asymmetry, and quantitative morphology differed by diagnosis, while behavioral analyses examined associations with inattention, hyperactivity-impulsivity, and cognitive measures. Age and gender were included as covariates. Results: Analyses revealed that, in both NT and ADHD individuals, there was significant leftward asymmetry in PCGS presence. Between groups, the PCGS was less likely to be present in individuals with ADHD in the left hemisphere. Leftward PCGS absence was also associated with significantly higher ADHD index and hyperactivity-impulsivity scores. Conclusions: These findings advance understanding of how early neurodevelopmental variation in cortical folding may serve as a structural intermediary between genetic liability and the behavioral expression of ADHD.
observations.title: Linking anterior cingulate sulcal variability to attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder behavior

metadata.summary: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) commonly coexists with atrial fibrillation (AF), but shared mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we hypothesized that Pitx2, a transcription factor located near the strongest genetic locus associated with AF in humans, increases susceptibility to HFpEF-like remodeling. We also sought to understand pathways that might be central to this increased risk. Male and female Pitx2+/− mice and wild-type littermates received 3-week subcutaneous osmotic pump infusion of saline or angiotensin II (Ang II; 500 ng/kg/min). Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and catheterization, and functional capacity by exercise treadmill. RNA transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify candidate pathways. In a separate cohort, Ang II–treated mice were randomized to oral GKT136901 (30 mg/kg/day) or vehicle during infusion. After Ang II infusion, Pitx2+/− mice developed exaggerated HFpEF-like changes, including greater left ventricular hypertrophy, left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction, elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and reduced treadmill performance. RNA-seq showed enrichment of metabolic and stress-response pathways with selective upregulation of Nox4, confirmed by RT-qPCR. GKT136901 attenuated structural remodeling, diastolic dysfunction indices, elevated filling pressures, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, but did not improve endurance. These findings implicate redox signaling, including Nox4, in AF genetic susceptibility–HFpEF interactions.

observations.text:
ObjectivesSocial media trends such as the "Benadryl Challenge" have increased adolescent misuse of diphenhydramine (DPH), an over-the-counter antihistamine with anticholinergic activity. Whether co-ingested anticholinergic medications compound cardiac risk is untested. Using the Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) scale, this study examined whether co-medication ACB burden is associated with outcome severity and cardiac toxicity in adolescent DPH cases reported to the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS).

MethodsThis study extracted all adolescent reports (age 13-19) mentioning DPH in any drug role from AEMS, yielding 3,168 cases from 217,507 deduplicated records. Given non-normality (Shapiro-Wilk, all p < 0.001), non-parametric tests were used. A multivariable logistic regression predicted cardiac toxicity; logistic and random-forest models were compared by cross-validated AUC.

ResultsCo-medication ACB burden correlated positively with case severity ({rho} = 0.142, p < 0.001) and differed by age group (H = 19.52, p < 0.001). However, burden and cardiac risk diverged: cardiac cases carried a lower burden (mean 0.55 vs 1.27) and were younger, and burden did not independently predict cardiac toxicity (OR = 0.927, 95% CI [0.841, 1.022], p = 0.128). Younger age was the strongest predictor (OR = 0.865 per year, p < 0.001); cardiac events occurred in 10.2% of 13-15-year-olds versus 4.9% of older adolescents.

ConclusionAnticholinergic co-medication burden and cardiac risk dissociate: burden tracks overall severity, but cardiac events concentrate in the youngest, least co-medicated adolescents, a profile consistent with deliberate single-agent overdose rather than polypharmacy. A low co-medication burden should not reassure clinicians triaging young adolescents.
observations.title: Anticholinergic Co-Medication Burden Does Not Predict Cardiac Toxicity in Adolescent Diphenhydramine Exposure: A Pharmacovigilance Study of the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System

metadata.summary: Oncofetal programs are often co-opted in high-grade gliomas and represent tumor cell vulnerabilities for therapeutic exploitation. Here, we integrate single nucleus RNA-seq and single-cell ATAC sequencing data generated from germinal matrix and cortical plate regions macrodissected from prenatal and postnatal developing brain autopsy tissue, creating an expanded spatiotemporal multi-omic dataset of gliogenic progenitors. The integrated multi-omics data includes previously published data (Ramos et al, Nature Commun 2022; Herring et al, Cell 2022) as well as newly-generated and herein deposited data. We use this dataset to interrogate oncofetal cell state composition in grade 4 gliomas across several published high-grade glioma / glioblastoma (GBM) datasets to uniquely assess tumor heterogeneity related to infiltrative biology near the margin and disease recurrence, in addition to genomic drivers. Our analyses reveal the preferential enrichment of glial intermediate progenitor cell (gIPC)-like cell state in GBM, most reminiscent of third-trimester germinal matrix gIPC progenitors, across tumor regions and in recurrence, irrespective of EGFR amplification status.

observations.text: Advances in high-throughput mesoscale microscopy and machine learning-based image analysis pipelines have made unbiased whole-brain imaging widely accessible. However, translating the resulting atlas-mapped datasets into biologically meaningful results remains a substantial barrier owing to their sheer magnitude and complex hierarchical organization. Consequently, reporting structure and analysis methods vary widely across studies, undermining rigor and reproducibility. To address this, we developed a user-friendly data reduction workflow, HERO (Hierarchy-aware Expression Region Organization), designed to perform hierarchy-aware selection, refinement, ranking, and visualization of whole-brain cell detection datasets. The workflow is customizable to specific needs, requires minimal coding experience, and outputs transparent, curated results. HERO functions as a seamless plug-in within larger-scale whole-brain cell detection analysis pipelines, providing efficient, unbiased region selection to streamline subsequent statistical analyses and comparative evaluations. Although HERO is developed with mouse cell-detection datasets, it can be applied to any atlas-mapped dataset that contains hierarchical information. Here, we applied the HERO pipeline to example cell detection datasets containing afferent cells from the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BST) and the insular cortex (insula). HERO provided top projecting regions consistent with historical tracing studies for the BST (e.g., amygdalar and hypothalamic regions) and the insula (e.g., somatosensory, autonomic, and interoceptive regions). Furthermore, the refinement step of HERO provides additional enriched regions originally obscured in the primary ranked outputs, such as memory- and emotion-associated structures. With HEROs dynamic processing, we were able to identify top-projecting regions consistent with the literature and, additionally, find regions often obscured in these large datasets. In sum, HERO offers a standardized analysis workflow to reduce whole-brain cell-detection datasets, transforming raw regional cell counts into curated results and advancing the effectiveness, interpretability, and accessibility of whole-brain imaging in neuroscience.
observations.title: HERO: A hierarchy-aware analysis pipeline for reducing and refining whole-brain atlas-mapped cellular datasets

metadata.summary: Degenerative mitral valve disease (DMVD) is a highly prevalent cardiac condition characterized by mitral valve interstitial cell (MVIC) activation and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. To investigate the transcriptional reprogramming underlying these processes, we performed RNA sequencing on an established three-dimensional (3D) porcine MVIC-collagen (VIC-COL) model.Following a 14-day maturation period, the constructs were treated with transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) for an additional 14 days, while untreated constructs cultured for the same duration served as controls. Samples were prepared from cells derived from three independent biological replicates (i.e. mitral valves from three different pigs). For each replicate, three constructs were pooled as one sample for final analysis. The analysis identified 915 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), revealing a significant transcriptional shift. Specifically, TGF-β1 led to a predominant upregulation of immune and inflammatory networks, including the IL-6/JAK/STAT3, TNF-α/NF-κB, and NOD-like receptor pathways, alongside processes associated with extracellular matrix organization, cell-cell adhesion, cell adhesion regulation, and cellular senescence. Furthermore, cross-species transcriptomic comparisons with a clinical canine DMVD dataset confirmed the conservation of these immune-centric signatures. Collectively, our findings suggest that immune-inflammatory signaling may act as a key modulator of ECM remodeling associated with MVIC activation. Moreover, the 3D VIC-COL system established in this study can serve as a reliable in vitro platform for investigating MVIC activation, ECM remodeling, and immune-related pathway changes in DMVD pathogenesis.

observations.text: AlphaFold3 represents a major advance in protein structure prediction, yet its performance on intrinsically disordered proteins remains uncharacterized. We present the first systematic evaluation of AF3 on disordered systems, revealing a striking dichotomy. For monomers, AF3's pLDDT scores reliably predict disorder (MCC: 0.693), matching AlphaFold2 and rivaling dedicated predictors. This consistency across fundamentally different architectures confirms that disorder prediction emerges from training data, not model design. For multimers, the picture grows complex. Despite comparable aggregate performance (mean DockQ: 0.563 vs 0.571), AF3 and AF2 achieve these results through fundamentally different mechanisms. Conventional structural features explain 58% of AF2's variance but only 42% of AF3's. Users cannot predict when AF3 will succeed or fail from interface properties alone. On disorder-to-order transitions (MFIB benchmark), both models perform equally well, successfully predicting final folded states. Yet seed variance analysis reveals AF3's failures are deterministic: the model converges to identical structures across independent runs, whether correct or incorrect, indicating rigid structural priors override available information. Our findings establish AF3 as reliable for the prediction of monomer disorder but unpredictable for multimers. Architectural innovation alone cannot overcome training data bias. Progress demands disorder-enriched datasets and ensemble sampling, not merely novel architectures.
observations.title: AlphaFold3 and Intrinsically Disordered Proteins: Reliable Monomer Prediction, Unpredictable Multimer Performance

The data were used to evaluate transcriptional remodeling in S. aureus during LAB exposure and the adaptive responses of LAB during interaction with S. aureus biofilms.
